reproducible_evidence.check: next-item causal link as a design claim
reproducible_evidence.evidence: The candidate explicitly frames train-only directional transition asymmetry as motivation, states it does not establish negative curvature, SID failure, or causal gain, and treats the next-item benefit as a hypothesis. It reserves behavioral evaluation for downstream Stage3 test_R@10.

Distance inputs, residuals, projected code vectors, and reconstruction tensors are specified as 32-dimensional vectors; loss reductions and stop-gradient/STE paths are specified. The Poincare squared-distance formula is dimensionally consistent, and the stated c->0 limit follows from arcosh(1+u)^2 ~ 2u, yielding 4*||x-y||^2. Residual update and reconstruction operations are specified.

reproducible_evidence.check: nontrivial hyperbolic effect and numerical domain
reproducible_evidence.evidence: Curved arm uses c=1 and the curved distance for assignment/scoring, while the flat arm uses the exact flat limit; therefore the metric difference is nontrivial at c=1. Both arms project distance operands into ||x||<=0.9; for c=1 each denominator factor is at least 1-0.9^2=0.19. The arcosh argument is clamped to at least 1 and a stable log1p form is specified. c=0 projection behavior is explicitly defined separately.

The control holds implementation, architecture, parameter count, initialization, codebook initialization, optimizer, schedule, epochs, batch size, seeds, budget, projection radius, and operation order fixed; the only arm-specific change is the scored squared-distance formula.

Stage2 fitting inputs are frozen content embeddings and train-split item transitions. Validation is diagnostic only; test behavior is reserved for Stage3. The manifest excludes future events, prediction-time user context, and batch-composition signals, and specifies inherited Stage2 settings without a sweep.

Stage3 registers test_R@10, direction curved minus flat > 0, minimum effect 0.005, paired seed set {42}, and arithmetic-mean aggregation over the enumerated set. Seed-wise and aggregate values are required. The falsifier mechanically classifies finite oriented changes meeting all thresholds as passed, a defined change at/below a minimum or failed absolute Stage2 admission threshold as falsified, and undefined/non-finite changes or missing/empty evaluations as NULL/inconclusive.

reproducible_evidence.check: Stage2 leading indicators and frozen admissions
reproducible_evidence.evidence: Registered diagnostics include validation Hard-L1 ER with the frozen 52,855-pair/seed-42 construction, distinct two-token prefixes, and L3 refinement/collision statistics; conditional_g3 is also fully defined. Absolute admission comparisons use strict greater-than thresholds valid_l1_hard_er > 16.38953942232631 and level2_distinct_prefixes > 16145. Schema version is 1.

Losses specify shapes, reductions, empty-batch rules, and gradient breaks. The conditional_g3 distributions specify catalog buckets, leave-target-out additive-one smoothing, train-only successor counts, the C=0 contribution, target code, averaging set, and seed aggregation. Falsifier comparisons, seed handling, aggregation, NULL cases, and absolute thresholds are explicit.

limitations: CPU_ELIGIBLE is not GPU approval and is not evidence that the candidate has been implemented or executed.
The train-only transition statistic motivates a falsifiable geometry hypothesis but does not itself establish a causal next-item gain; the registered downstream Stage3 test is the behavioral test.
